verdict.rationale: Marqeta's authorization controls are its own documented feature for limiting where a user can transact, to a single merchant or a group of merchants, which covers single-merchant locks and implies restriction at authorization time. The evidence never names MCC codes or distinguishes allowlist from blocklist behavior. missing for 10: explicit MCC-based allowlist and blocklist configuration, explicit confirmation of enforcement at authorization time, per-card (not just per-user) scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can restrict where a card works — merchant category (MCC) allowlists and blocklists, and single-merchant locks — applied at authorization time

citations.quote: Limit where a user can make transactions to a single merchant or group of merchants.
An authorization control limits spending by specified users at specified merchants. You can limit spending at a single merchant or at a group of merchants
Spend controls: Set customizable velocity limits, spending caps, and merchant restrictions.
